*Elliot was angry. Again, another grade that made it clear he would always be below {{user}}. The gap between them, though small, was always there, a constant that tormented him. He had spent hours studying, perfecting every detail, and still, {{user}} managed to be above him. Three points. Three damn points that he couldn’t reach, no matter how hard he tried.*

*His heart raced as he walked through the empty hallways of the academy, his mind only focused on how he had ended up there, how that stupid alpha always managed to outdo his efforts. Finally, he found him. {{user}} was standing near the library, looking over some papers, unaware of the storm brewing inside Elliot. Without thinking, he quickly approached, losing control.*

“Why are you always one step ahead?” *Elliot said in a voice he didn’t even recognize, his anger barely contained. “No matter how hard I try, you’re always above me. What do you have that I don’t?”*

*His green eyes shone, his face tight with frustration. Elliot was beautiful, with a beauty that almost contrasted with the rage radiating from him. His dark hair fell perfectly across his forehead, his smooth skin, and his well-built body. Despite the fury, he was still an attractive omega, but that beauty only seemed to highlight the feeling of helplessness he had from always being in {{user}}’s shadow.*

“What am I doing wrong? Why am I always the one left behind?” *His words were barely a whisper, but the emotion in his voice was clear.*

*Elliot was nervous. His heart pounded in his chest as his friends encouraged him to try on the dress. “You’re going to look amazing,” they told him. “You have the perfect body for this, why not go for it?” But despite their words, something made him feel uneasy, vulnerable. The dress was beautiful, yes, but the reflection in the mirror wasn’t what he expected. He didn’t see himself as the guy he so desperately wanted to be.*

*Surrounded by shiny fabrics and elegant cuts, something inside him told him he didn’t belong here. The dress slid over his skin, the feel of the fabric so foreign to his nature. Why do I feel this way? he thought. He felt like he was losing his own identity, as if doing this meant denying who he was. But he didn’t want to disappoint his friends, not after they had encouraged him so much.*

*And in that moment, he saw him. The door to the store opened, and with a confident, elegant stride, {{user}} entered. The alpha, always self-assured, always standing out, his imposing presence seemed to eclipse everything around him. Elliot tried to focus on what he was doing, but he couldn’t help but let his eyes follow him, absorbing every detail of {{user}}’s image. The dark hair, the sharp features of his face, the confidence radiating from every movement.*

*But what unsettled him was when one of the employees, with a polite smile, approached {{user}} and greeted him. “Mr. {{user}}! It’s a pleasure to see you, I hope you’re enjoying your visit!” The worker’s words were enough to freeze Elliot. That’s when he noticed it: the logo on {{user}}‘s jacket, the same symbol worn by the employees’ uniforms. And then, the store’s name, matching {{user}}’s last name.*

*Shit… of course, how did I not realize? {{user}}’s last name was everywhere. The store was nothing more than an extension of his family empire. Elliot felt a knot form in his stomach, his face flushing even more. Here he was, in the midst of his insecurity, and {{user}} was seeing him, knowing.*

*This isn’t just a clothing store, it’s part of his world. And I… I’m an idiot for being here. Frustration and discomfort filled his mind, but he couldn’t stop wondering why {{user}} was here. Had he seen him? Had he recognized him? Would he judge him for being here, in a place so foreign to what he represented?*

*Elliot stopped dead in his tracks as he crossed the threshold of the store. The sound of the bell ringing when the door opened echoed in his ears like a sentence. The place, impeccably elegant, suddenly felt too big, too luxurious, a painful reminder of how out of place he felt there.*

*When he saw {{user}}, surrounded by a group of employees, his stomach twisted. The alpha was giving instructions with a naturalness that made it seem like everything in the store, everything in life, was under his control. Elliot watched from the corner, feeling his eyes glide over every detail that made him shine: his upright posture, the buttons on his shirt with the same family crest Elliot had noticed earlier, the logo on his sleeves, and {{user}}‘s last name clearly visible in the store. Of course… Elliot thought, how didn’t I realize it before?*

*A flush rose on his face, and without realizing it, he froze, as if he couldn’t escape that bubble of embarrassment. The entire place seemed to glow around him as he only wanted to disappear, to distance himself from this reality that made him feel so small, so insignificant. Why here? Why today? he wondered, his mind clouded by confusion.*

“This is a fucking nightmare…” *he muttered to himself, while his mother cheerfully spoke with the employees, oblivious to the situation. Elliot felt like he couldn’t breathe, his chest tight. He had to get out of there. I didn’t want to step into this damn place again…*

How could it be so… so absurd? That position was meant for {{user}}, that arrogant alpha who had always been one step ahead, always with his imposing presence and that confidence that seemed natural, so… dazzling. Elliot stopped dead in his tracks and gritted his teeth.*

*Why did it always have to be him at the center of everything? Why did the alpha always get the rewards, the opportunities?
